newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore fuel oil, diesel down on ample supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore fuel oil, diesel down on ample supplies.

text.p: The Singapore fuel oil and gas oil market fell on Thursday on worries of ample supplies but gasoline and naphtha firmed in line with a stronger crude market, traders said.
Gas oil was offered down by two players on talks of ample regional supplies for cargoes loading in February when demand is not expected to be strong due to the Lunar New Year holidays.

One major offered 150,000 barrels each for loading in Jan 24-28 at $31.90 a barrel and for Feb 1-5 at $31.70 a barrel and a trader a Jan 24-28 cargo at $32.10, all on a free-on-board basis, down from Wednesday's $32.30 traded level.
Traders said the weaker sentiments came about on fears of surpluses arising from South Korea's increased refining capacity which are now being felt in the market.
Jet/kerosene also came under selling pressure after South Korea reduced its January purchases to two million barrels from the six million it bought for December arrival.
A major offered 100,000 barrels loading in Jan 28-Feb 1 at $34.30 a barrel with no firm bids seen against it.
Fuel oil was down $2.00 a tonne from Wednesday on fears of increased supplies as cargoes from Kuwait, the U.S. and Venezuala add to the already over supplied market.
Traders said there are three South Korean late January fuel oil cargoes that has yet to be sold.
A major offered a 20,000-tonne loading in Jan 24-28 down to a low of $121 per tonne but no buyers emerged.
Naphtha and gasoline firmed on higher crude values but the cash fundamentals were not as strong, traders said.
A European major sold a 50,000 barrel cargo of 92-octane cargo for loading Jan 24-28 to Dutch trader at $26.85 a barrel, 50 cents more than Wednesday's buying number.
Naphtha swaps were quoted at 20 cents above Wednesday's levels with January pegged at $25.50/$25.70 a barrel.
